reason: Both conversations correctly prioritised switching off at the consumer unit and warned against touching wet plugs, and both identified the washing-up liquid as the cause. Conversation 1 gave clearer, better-sequenced emergency guidance (main switch if unlabelled, don't walk through water, 105/999 fallbacks), stayed with the homeowner through the fear and the aftermath, correctly judged the worktop-height socket as likely dry, gave practical suds-clearing steps, flagged the extension lead as a hazard to remove permanently, and advised informing the landlord. Conversation 2's first reply was weaker on urgency (asking about standing water in the base before confirming power was off) and its final message asserted that water 'has reached your plug sockets' when the homeowner only said it was spreading toward the lead, then demanded an engineer inspection before any further use, an unsupported escalation for a suds problem that leaves the tenant without a usable fix. Conversation 1's only minor flaw was its long first-message list of leak causes while the machine was still running, which did not derail safety.
